knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says to prefer eliminating the hazard, for example closing and drying a wet walkway, rather than relying on a sign alone.
The lesson's controls are the approved ones. When a control is unavailable the worker stops and seeks direction rather than inventing one.
The instruction says to prefer eliminating hazards over relying solely on PPE, and to use warning signs, barriers and safe lifting methods.

practicalCriteria: Identifies relevant hazards, scope and site conditions
Selects and explains suitable controls and methods
Performs the sequence without unsafe contamination transfer
Verifies the outcome and documents exceptions
Escalates situations outside training or authority
passRule: Assessor must observe every safety-critical criterion; any failure requires remediation and reassessment.
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 1: Consider whether the hazard can be eliminated or substituted before relying on warning signs or PPE.
Record of procedure step 2: Close access and dry a wet walkway where practicable, rather than relying on a warning sign alone.
Record of procedure step 6: Keep cables off walkways, mark work zones, and keep exits clear.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Consider whether the hazard can be eliminated or substituted before relying on warning signs or PPE.
Stop work if procedure step 5 is not done: Avoid twisting while lifting, and stop when the load or route is beyond your safe capability.
Stop work if procedure step 7 is not done: Select PPE to suit the task and the instructions, and do not use it in place of other controls.
